data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel is more reliable specifically because the checklist decomposes the expert's implicit 'holistic' judgment into a set of independent Bernoulli trials, where the panel's aggregation reduces the variance of the error term.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist items are highly correlated, meaning a single misconception causes the entire panel to fail simultaneously.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition is a single-point-of-failure system; one cognitive slip leads to a wrong answer. A checklist decomposes the judgment into N independent binary checks. Even if non-experts are less accurate per check, the panel's consensus on these discrete steps creates a redundancy layer. The 'reliability' is an emergent property of the law of large numbers applied to the checklist's discrete components rather than the final judgment.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
